experiments.scope: Exact recount of the structural counts of the trail search P (proof 2.1) for start lanes 0, 1. Trial 0 runs T1 (the depth-first search of in-kernel cores of at most 10 bits) from bit (lane, z = 0) of each lane of the group, counting every node, and for each core found whose smallest lane is in the group computes C1 (alpha4 compatible with beta3 = T2 leaves), decides P45 > 0 exactly (pruned search over the same alpha4), and, if P45 > 0, computes C2 (beta2 compatible with alpha3) and the number of half vectors of T3's meet-in-the-middle split (rows 0..h-1 and h..n-1 of alpha3, h minimising the sum of the two products). PASS iff the per-lane node counts and the group totals equal GROUP_LOG. The groups 0..3 (lanes 0-1, 2-7, 8-16, 17-24) partition the cores. Other trials return no pair. PASS = (00^135, 01||00^134) satisfies the declared event; FAIL = (00^135, 02||00^134) does not. Both are fixed sentinels, so the host check is vacuous; the evidence is the organizer's execution of the visible code, and the host-counted numbers are successes (PASS) and returned_pairs (PASS + FAIL).
experiments.hypothesis: P's structural counts that enter the time bound are exact. Predicted: PASS with 692,664 nodes, 1023 cores, sum C1 = 974,737,408, 204 cores with P45 > 0, sum C2 = 608,900,651,514, 21,466,134 half vectors. Over the four groups (r5-trail-0, r5-trail-1, r5-trail-23): 8,674,833 nodes, 1741 cores, C1 = 1,639,088,128, 467 kept cores, C2 = 1,379,275,399,350 and 48,592,224 half vectors: the exact counts that P's charge multiplies by its prices (proof 2.1, 6).

experiments.scope: The B' program bprime() with the R5 constants (no attempt limit per candidate, DMIN 33, D2u weights 1), its budget and its per-candidate cap, both enforced by the counter WK (proof 2.2), executed whole; then R7's count (v20) and the connector with organizer coins. Trial 1 (B' at its budget and candidate cap) runs in r5-mitm-0 as its trial 1. Trial 2: PASS iff the table RUNS (v20: R7's) has 48 runs, 39 with an output (each with a status string of length i + 1), and the one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson lower bound of 39 of 48 (exact binomial tail, bisection) is at least 0.40. Trials 3..26: one connector attempt on trial 0's advice with the trial's organizer seed as coins; PASS iff accepted and verify_space holds (Lemmas 1-2 at two random points). Other trials return no pair. Sentinels and evidence as in r5-trail-0. (v17) Trial 0 also reports the true cost of that B' run (WK's cost with Aff's table-update and copy sites at their word cost, proof V.5) as an observation. (v25s: regrouped so that every process stays well inside the organizer's 20 s; see proof Z.6.)
experiments.hypothesis: Time bound and H1: B' stops each candidate at its cap and the run at its budget; the logged B' runs of R7 are the shipped program's runs; the success count of H1 is R7's table. (v17) The true cost of trial 0's B' run is below its WK cost. Predicted: PASS on trials 0 and 2 (trial 0 cost 16,446,246,658 or 13,220,514,578 or 11,331,166,259 for k = 6, 33, 37; trial 2: bound 0.6956); trials 3..26: descriptive acceptance (R7's label-seeded rate was 2400 of 6920 attempts). experiments.scope: Audit of the R7 study (proof W.2, Appendix F; v20), stratum 0 of 8: the R7 runs 1, 10, 19, 34, 42 (the 38 R7 runs with an output other than run 22 (our replay test measured a peak of 107.8 MB, too close to the sandbox's 128 MB; the collision is in R7's per-run ledger), in k order, stratum = position mod 8). Trial 0 picks run L[q0], q0 = SHA-256(trial 0 seed) mod n (v25s: one run per stratum and review; v25 replayed two). For the picked run k (table RUNS: advice (c, j, DF, hash), first positive space idx, accepting attempt i, coordinate, DF of the space, status string of connector attempts 0..i): B' re-derives the advice from the label 'hashsmash sha3-256-r5 R7 run k' (candidate setup c, attempt j; accepted with the logged DF and advice hash; facts of proof 3); the status string must end with an accepted attempt, contain exactly idx accepted attempts and idx <= K = 50; the connector attempts i and min(i, 23) others drawn from 0..i-1 with the trial seed (all of 0..i if i < 24) are re-run with the run's coins (label || 'conn' || c + 1, attempt index) and must give the logged status of each; attempt i must be accepted with the logged DF; then the Python E (e_window) runs on the 2^12 aligned coordinates containing the logged coordinate. The trial returns E's first output if every check passes and the output is at the logged coordinate, otherwise no pair. Other trials return no pair. (v25s: regrouped so that every process stays well inside the organizer's 20 s; see proof Z.6.) In production the seeds are the organizer's; a holdout nonce changes the picked runs and attempts.
experiments.hypothesis: H1 numerator: the successes in the R7 table are outputs of v20's algorithm (B', connector rule, E) run from their labels, at the logged place among the advice's 50 accepted spaces. Predicted: 1 full 5-round collision of two distinct 135-byte messages.

For the picked run k (table RUNS: advice (c, j, DF, hash), first positive space idx, accepting attempt i, coordinate, DF of the space, status string of connector attempts 0..i): B' re-derives the advice from the label 'hashsmash sha3-256-r5 R7 run k' (candidate setup c, attempt j; accepted with the logged DF and advice hash; facts of proof 3); the status string must end with an accepted attempt, contain exactly idx accepted attempts and idx <= K = 50; the connector attempts i and min(i, 23) others drawn from 0..i-1 with the trial seed (all of 0..i if i < 24) are re-run with the run's coins (label || 'conn' || c + 1, attempt index) and must give the logged status of each; attempt i must be accepted with the logged DF; then the Python E (e_window) runs on the 2^12 aligned coordinates containing the logged coordinate. The trial returns E's first output if every check passes and the output is at the logged coordinate, otherwise no pair. Other trials return no pair. (v25s: regrouped so that every process stays well inside the organizer's 20 s; see proof Z.6.) In production the seeds are the organizer's; a holdout nonce changes the picked runs and attempts.
experiments.hypothesis: H1 numerator: the successes in the R7 table are outputs of v20's algorithm (B', connector rule, E) run from their labels, at the logged place among the advice's 50 accepted spaces. Predicted: 1 full 5-round collision of two distinct 135-byte messages.
